title: inlet-sdk-for-async-request-telemetry-and-deterministic-context-parenting
creator: Sofia Garcia
description: Background: We need a low-cost way to guarantee trace continuity for highly asynchronous request patterns (worker queues, serverless forks, background jobs) without requiring heavy SDK changes in every language. Current gaps: 1) parent/child assignment loses lineage when requests spawn detached goroutines/tasks; 2) sampling hints are frequently dropped by intermediary proxies; 3) lightweight language runtimes (edge binaries) can't bear high allocation instrumentation. Goal: Build an "inlet" SDK component and middleware adapters that provide deterministic parent assignment and loss-tolerant propagation with minimal per-request overhead. The inlet should be usable as: - middleware for HTTP/gRPC frameworks (Node/Express, Python/Flask/FastAPI, Go net/http, Java/Ktor) - a lightweight client-side library to attach to job payloads (queue messages, cron triggers) - an unobtrusive runtime hook that rehydrates context for async continuations Key design constraints: keep p99 CPU/time overhead < 0.5ms for typical tiny requests, avoid allocations on hot path, be opt-in via config flags, respect existing sampling policies and preserve Baggage semantics. This ticket covers design, prototype SDKs for Node and Go, middleware adapters, and updating observability dashboards to measure continuity.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic parent assignment algorithm implemented and documented (algorithm + pseudo-code)
Node and Go inlet SDK prototypes integrated with Express and net/http examples
End-to-end tests showing trace continuity for spawn/fanout patterns (HTTP -> queue -> worker -> background flush)
Performance regression: median overhead <0.2ms, p99 overhead <0.5ms on our benchmark harness
Sampling hint propagation success rate > 99% across simulated proxy chains
Dashboards updated: new panels for Missing-Parent%, Trace-Continuation-Rate, Inlet-Overhead histogram
Feature gated and toggleable via runtime flag; gradually rolled out to 10% -> 50% -> 100%
Documentation + migration notes for SDK consumers and guidance for platform teams
technical_notes: Core idea: introduce an "inlet token" that is a compact, signed context envelope (base64 URL-safe) carrying minimal fields: parent_id (optional), deterministic_seed, sampling_hint, and an integrity HMAC. Deterministic parenting: when an async worker spawns without an explicit parent, the inlet computes a stable parent candidate as H(deterministic_seed, spawn_site_id) so that retries/follow-ups re-associate to the same logical trace. Integrity and backwards compatibility: middleware will accept either standard trace headers or inlet tokens; if both present inlet takes precedence only when the sampled trace is unknown. Implementation specifics: - allocate-once buffer for header parsing to avoid per-request allocations in hot path - provide two integration layers: passive (read-only header normalizer) and active (inject/re-hydrate and sign) - fall back to existing sampler if inlet token missing - expose binding for C/edge runtimes via a tiny shim API (C ABI) Trade-offs: deterministic parenting increases chance of false-positive parent assignment in highly-parallel fanout; mitigation includes probabilistic threshold and "split-trace" hint in headers. We will iterate after measuring continuity vs correctness.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design/prototype, 2 weeks): finalize token format and deterministic algorithm; implement Node + Go prototypes. Phase 1 (canary, 1 week): enable for internal services traffic only (10% sample), monitor metrics. Phase 2 (expanded rollout, 2 weeks): enable for platform customers in sandbox; add opt-out flags. Phase 3 (GA): library publish, docs, and enable-by-default for new clusters. Safety: kill-switch env var and runtime toggle in Console; automated rollback if Missing-Parent% increases by >1pp or p99 latency overhead regresses beyond threshold.
testing: Unit tests for token encoding/decoding and HMAC validation. Integration tests covering: spawn -> queue -> worker flows, header normalization across proxy chains, and sampling hint propagation. Performance tests run on the bench harness with 100k synthetic requests to validate p50/p95/p99 overhead. Chaos tests to simulate dropped headers and concurrent fanout to validate deterministic parenting doesn't cause pathological joins.
